text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Politburo member Nong Duc Manh opened the National Assembly's autumn session on Tuesday.
-- Vietnam will seek investment capital equivalent to about 29 percent of Gross National Product next year, lower than the 30 percent stipulated in its five-year-plan.
-- Farmers in the Mekong Delta have called for a government policy to regulate grain prices.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told reporters Vietnam has basically achieved its socio-economic targets this year, but more time is needed to overcome a range of problems including teenage drug abuse.
-- Vietnam launched a nationwide anti-drug campaign in schools and colleges on Tuesday.
-- Philippine's army commander C.P. Mariano visited Vietnam last week to strengthen relations and mutual understanding.
-- Flooding and storms in the Mekong Delta have killed 63 people, left 12 missing and more than 39,000 families in need of help.
-- Revenue from state-owned industry in Hanoi has reached only 45 percent of its annual target so far this year. The sector exported goods worth $20 million in the first nine months.
-- Algerian President Liamine Zeroual will arrive in Vietnam on October 21st for a three-day friendship visit.
-- Water levels in upstream areas of the Mekong Delta have fallen slightly, but lower stretches are still suffering serious flooding.
-- Rock star Sting and his 28-member group with 13 tonnes of equipment has arrived Ho Chi Minh City to perform in a Wednesday night concert.
